problems.source_says: Not supported. The codebook reserves online_rct for randomized experiments with people (section 4). The document calls S1 a preregistered 2 x 3 between-subjects design in which writers worked 'in one of three conditions', but no passage in the 29 pages says how writers were allocated to the GenAI conditions or that allocation was random. The class also conflicts with the form's own assignment block (randomized = not_stated), and the form's reconciliation already marks this field confirmed: false.
problems.quote: The writing task followed a 2 × 3 between-subjects design, crossing writer background (L1 vs. L2) with GenAI usage (human-only vs. AI ideation vs. AI refinement).
problems.locator: p. 17, Materials and Methods, Writing task and materials; creativity-codebook.md section 4

problems.field: studies[S1].assignment.randomized and eligibility.criterion_1_random_assignment_of_ai (conclusion under test: writers were randomly assigned to GenAI assistance)
problems.form_value: Conclusion under test: randomized. The form itself codes assignment.randomized = not_stated and criterion_1 = unclear.
problems.source_says: The document gives no allocation rule for the GenAI conditions. The only randomization of the writers' session is the order of the four scenarios. Every other use of 'random' or 'assign' concerns evaluator presentation order (p. 16), the evaluators' rating instruction (p. 18), random intercepts and random-effects rows (p. 19; Tab. S1-S3, pp. 28-29), or the LLM-judge sample (Fig. S10, p. 27). Fig. 1 draws arrows from the L1 and L2 writer groups to the three conditions with no allocation label. The preregistered target of '100 per cell' (p. 16) shows that the cells were planned, not how writers entered them. The claim of random assignment therefore has no support in the text.
problems.quote: All writers responded to the same four scenarios, presented in a randomized order
problems.locator: p. 17, Writing task and materials; text-layer search of pp. 1-29 for random*, assign*, allocat*, counterbalanc*, quota, stratif*; page images pp. 1-29, Fig. 1 on p. 5

confirmed.statement: The form's assignment.randomized = not_stated is right. No passage says writers were randomly assigned. In the text layer, 'random' appears only for scenario order (p. 17), evaluator presentation order (p. 16), random intercepts (p. 19), random-effects rows (Tab. S1-S3), and the LLM-judge sample (Fig. S10). 'Assign' appears only in the evaluator instructions (p. 18).
confirmed.locator: pp. 16, 17, 18, 19, 27, 28-29; text-layer search of all 29 pages and page-by-page reading of the PDF

confirmed.statement: Fig. 1 (study design) shows L1 and L2 writers branching to Human-only, AI ideation, and AI refinement. Its caption says writers 'completed four creative metaphor tasks either without AI, with AI-generated ideas (AI ideation), or with AI polishing their own ideas (AI refinement)'. Neither the figure nor the caption names an allocation method.

The authors varied the GenAI condition across writers ('to vary how much of each idea originated from humans, participants generated metaphors in one of three conditions'). Nothing in the text says writers picked their condition. The only self-chosen feature is the language of AI interaction for L2 writers in the two AI arms.
confirmed.locator: pp. 4-5, Introduction; p. 17, Writing task and materials; p. 18, Language of AI interaction

confirmed.statement: What differs across conditions is GenAI help with the writer's own metaphor: five GPT-4o candidate metaphors with explanations before composing (AI ideation), or five GPT-4o candidate explanations for a metaphor the writer composed first (AI refinement). Diversity and ratings are scored on what each writer submitted, so the conditions do not differ only in whose output is evaluated.
confirmed.locator: p. 17, AI ideation condition; pp. 17-18, AI refinement condition; p. 18, Evaluation task and Collective diversity measure

confirmed.statement: The tool is generative AI: GPT-4o (gpt-4o-2024-08-06) with the system prompts in SI Figs. S5-S8. The markdown misprints the version on p. 17 as 'gpt-4o-2024-0806'. The PDF reads gpt-4o-2024-08-06 on both p. 17 and p. 18.

The comparison arms match the form. Human-only writers wrote 'with no GenAI assistance provided or allowed at any stage', enforced by tab-switch detection (24 sessions terminated), so ai = none and ai_vs_bau fit. AI refinement vs. AI ideation is another AI configuration, so ai_design fits (the codebook lists 'ideas versus refinement').
confirmed.locator: p. 17, Human-only condition; pp. 17-18; creativity-codebook.md section 5

confirmed.statement: The design is between subjects, so check (e) on the order of conditions does not apply. The randomized order covers the four scenarios within each writer's session, not the GenAI conditions. The form's structure = between is right.

Writer background is recruited, not assigned. L1 and L2 writers entered through different Prolific eligibility criteria (L1 n = 318, L2 n = 326). L2 writers in the AI arms chose their language of AI interaction (84 of 228 chose their native language). The form treats both as non-randomized, which is right.
confirmed.locator: p. 16, Participants (Writers); p. 8; p. 17; p. 18, Language of AI interaction

confirmed.statement: The form's flag on Fig. S8 holds. The printed AI refinement prompt for L2 participants tells the model to 'provide 5 suggestion pairs of the first and second blanks', word for word the L2 ideation prompt of Fig. S6, while the L1 refinement prompt (Fig. S7) forbids hints for the metaphor. What L2 writers in the refinement arm received is uncertain, but it was GPT-4o help either way, so the AI-versus-no-AI contrast for criterion 1 is unaffected.
confirmed.locator: pp. 26-27, Figs. S6, S7, and S8

confirmed.statement: The form's assignment quote (p. 17) and its pp. 4-5 locator phrase ('participants generated metaphors in one of three conditions') are verbatim.
S2 assigns no people. It builds a persona prompt from each S1 writer's background questionnaire and was not preregistered, so randomized = no and design_class ai_vs_human are right.
confirmed.locator: p. 19, LLM simulation of the writer pool; p. 20, Preregistration and deviations

summary: The 29-page document never says how writers were allocated to the human-only, AI ideation, and AI refinement conditions, and its only randomization of the writers' session is the order of the four scenarios, so the online_rct class and the conclusion that writers were randomly assigned have no textual support. The conditions do differ in GPT-4o help on each writer's own metaphors against an enforced no-AI arm, and nothing suggests writers chose their condition, so criterion 1 stays unclear until the preregistration (https://tinyurl.com/DiverseCreativity) or the OSF materials show the allocation method.
